title: reference.json (site-studio)
description: The keys of one `content/references/<name>/reference.json` of a site-studio site at schema 9: the closed key set, the required `url` and `title`, text values, one-line values, the `url` scheme and the length limits. `fetched` is the address the page was fetched from. It cannot state what only the build can see: that a `project` names a piece, that `type` and `channel` are in the site's own lists (`references.types`, `references.channels` in site/site.json), that an `image` is a file that exists (a path that climbs out of the folder through `..` is the build's too), that no `card` file sits beside `image`, and the site's declared `schema` (a key marked schema 4, 5 or 9 is refused below that schema). The build is the check either way. A `$schema` key is not accepted in a reference.json.

kind.description: what sort of page it is

image.description: the card image: a path inside the reference's own folder, such as `media/preview.jpg`; used instead of a `card` file, and naming both is refused (schema 4)

role.description: one line on what you did, printed on every card of the reference (schema 4)

fetched.description: the address the page was fetched from; adopt puts the template's `captured_from` here; stored, never printed (schema 4; a date written under the older wording still builds)

author.description: who wrote the page; printed through the optional `reference-card.author` part of your own look (0.8.0), never otherwise (schema 4)

imageAlt.description: one line: the alt of the reference's card picture, on every card of it (schema 5)

imagePosition.description: a CSS position such as `center 30%`: that picture's `object-position` (schema 5)

project.description: the piece this reference is for: a piece's folder name (`harbor-lights`), or `<portfolio>/<folder>` when two portfolios hold that name; a name that matches no piece is refused. One line; a blank value reads as absent (schema 9)

type.description: what the page is, in a word or two, such as `Post` or `Film`; one line of at most 80 characters, and one of `references.types` when the site sets that list. Printed through the optional `reference-card.type` part of your own look, never otherwise; a blank value reads as absent (schema 9)

channel.description: where its audience saw it, whatever host the address names, such as `Instagram`; one line of at most 80 characters, and one of `references.channels` when the site sets that list. Printed through the optional `reference-card.channel` part of your own look, never otherwise; a blank value reads as absent (schema 9)
